questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to study abroad mainly to better my chances of being granted acces to a specific master's degree. However, I also studied abroad to explore new cultures, meet new people, and to hike - a lot.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Everything was made super easy for the exchange people in general. On the day of move-in, we were pretty much guided through the whole thing. 

Don't expect to hear a lot from the university till a week or two before move-in. They were awefully quite till right before school start, which is fine, if you know not to expect hearing anything from them.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Busses took students straight to their housing accomidations, after which several meetings were held about living in residence.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Four-bedroom apartments, one-bedroom apartments and a few other options with shared toilets I believe. I lived in a four-bedroom apartment which was great.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Apartments without kitchens have mandatory mealplans. I like to cook myself, so I didn't apply for those. I haven't actually tried the dining hall, however, I was told from multiple students that bought it, it wasn't worth it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Really consider living on campus in four-bedroom apartments. The exchange group at my semester abroad became quite close-knit, and living alone might make it more difficult to fully engage socially. I actually prioritised living alone, but ended up in a four-bedroom apartment with a brittish person, a scottish person and an Aussie. I am very happy I didn't live alone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration can be quite daunting. I ended up having to apply for merit multiple times because the courses available changed or because i didn't get a specific pre-requisite waived. I think the biggest issue is how long UCPH sometimes take to answer. Appart from that, things went smooth enough.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I personally don't really know. I never felt the coordinator was very helpful. However, course instructors at UBCO really wanted to help me get into the courses i prioritised, so I had a lot of help from them.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I decided to utilise my selectiveness studying a mix of biology and health and exercise science at UBCO. This deffinitely complicated things a lot. UCPH was completely fine with me doing this, however, UBCO were very confused with why a sport science student would apply for biology courses. I applied for "molecular genetics" but didnt get in, so I ended up studying "priciples in genetics" which was a fantastic and challening course. 

Appart from that, I got into all the courses I wanted to attend. Also, if you plan on applying for courses only within your specific education, I dont think you will have any issues with registration.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for 10 courses, even though you only need 4 courses to be a full-time student. This gives you a back-up in case you wont be granted access to a specific course. Also, really make sure you take time and control your timetable. A lot of students didn't spend the time planning their timetable, resulting in them not being able to attend the courses they had planned to attend.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Prepare yourself for a lot more testing than at UCPH. It is not uncommon for you to have two midterms, one final exam, and some kind of participation/assignment marked work, which all counts toward your final grade.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The courses I attended in HES were not as difficult as I was used to at UCPH. 

The courses I attended in BIOL were quite challening, but i expected this, attending biology courses without a background in biology. If you work hard, you can still do really well.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very hard to say. The style of teaching varied greatly between the instructors. Some wants you to engage actively will have you do presentations, others read of powerpoint slides the whole lecture.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
HES383 - Physical Dimensions of Ageing
HES 380 - Exercise metabolism
BIOL 300 - Advanced Cell Biology
BIOL 265 - Principles in Genetics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
HES 380 - Exercise metabolism
The course instructor, Jonathan Little, was an increadible teacher. I deffinitely recommend taking this course, if you are interrested in metabolism. 

BIOL 265 - Principles in Genetics
Extremely challening and busy course, however, if you are interested in genetics and are willing to work hard, you will learn a great deal from Dr. D'Souza.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None. I would however recommend bringing an appropriate amount of money for all the recreational stuff you want to do. It is not cheap to go to the rockies every other weekend, haha.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out for dinner is cheap. Groceries are a little more expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are clubs for everything at UBCO. Me and my flatmates didn't join them though, since we wanted to do other stuff thn what the clubs offered.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to Vancouver Island, Bannf, Jasper, Kootenay Mountain Range. My greatest memories of BC were made in those places.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: We rented a cabin in the Kootenay Mountains for 5 days. Unreal cozyness with a view. Do that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Very easy. To be fair, I didn't spend too much time with canadians as my flatmates were from the UK and Australia and out culture were very similar. 

I did of course meet canadians, and it wasn't a challenge to adjust, because I didn't have to adjust much to engage in those conversations.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go and talk to people. Everyone thinks it's cool your from abroad and even more how well me danes speak english. If your nervous about it, remember how far away from home are and how cool it is that you put yourself on this journey. Now is the time to find that new you ;)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I prefer fewer and really close friendships and I dont care much for superficial relations. Throughout all my time at the UBCO, game nights and movie nights were held for people to mingle. I really dont care much for those types of events, and I always find those things hard. Luckily my flatmates became my best friends in Canada, so we stopped going quite early.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The general feeling of hospitality and that everyone greets each other. I really like that.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: As mentioned earlier, my number one motivation to go was academic, however, remember to prioritise doing all the stuff you cant do at home. Go see nature. Make those new international friendships that will last you forever. Dont worry too much about your grades as they wont count on your danish transcript ( at least the didn't for me)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really, no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing incredible nature and meeting people that I now consider my friend. It is a special feeling looking at a world map, knowing a have friends in Spain, Norway, England, Scotland, Netherland, Australia, Canada, US, etc. I did not have that before my exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting to the rockies as often as we wanted to. If you have the money, consider buying a car. It will make everything so much easier.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You won't regret going!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
